summary: This work enhances superconducting qubit readout fidelity by exploiting two-mode squeezed states generated at the signal and idler frequencies of a nondegenerate Josephson mixer, coherently combining simultaneous measurements to amplify the qubit-encoded quadrature while suppressing noise. The scheme achieves fidelity improvements of 2–6% for practical gains (2–13 dB) and noise levels (8–50 photons), with improvements of 0.05–0.25% remaining possible above 99.5% fidelity at $G = 20$ dB, without requiring hardware changes or in-situ phase matching.
motivation: Standard dispersive readout of superconducting qubits using phase-preserving quantum-limited amplifiers (Josephson parametric amplifiers, traveling-wave parametric amplifiers) suffers from noise added by subsequent amplification stages in realistic output chains, which typically contain 3–10 dB insertion loss and elevates effective added noise to 20–100 photons at the HEMT input, motivating methods to further enhance readout SNR.
method: A cQED device with a transmon qubit coupled to a superconducting readout resonator outputs measurements amplified by a three-wave Josephson mixer (JM) with gain $G = 1.3$–4 dB and added noise ≈0.5 photons. Measurements at both output ports $a$ and $b$ (signal and idler at frequencies $f_a = 7.23$ GHz and $f_b = 9.71$ GHz) are simultaneously acquired, rotated by a relative phase $\phi$ to optimize SNR, then coherently combined by adding the rotated quadratures $(I_a + I_b^{\text{rot}}, Q_a + Q_b^{\text{rot}})$ to antisqueeze the qubit-carrying quadrature.
result: At fixed $\bar{n}_{\text{in}} = 90$, the combined mode achieves maximum assignment fidelity $F_{ab,\max} > 0.99$ vs $F_a \approx 0.985$ for single-mode readout; power SNR enhancements exceed a factor of two at $G = 2.3$–4 dB (e.g., $R_{ab,\max}/R_a = 1.66$ at $G = 8$ dB and $N_{\text{sys}} = 50$ photons); and $\Delta F = F_{ab,\max} - F_a$ remains positive for all practical gains $G > 1$ dB and noise $N_{\text{sys}} > 0.5$ photons.
